newsitem.title: USA: Kennedy seeks another minimum wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Kennedy seeks another minimum wage hike.

text.p: Sen. Edward Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat, Friday unveiled a bill to raise the minimum wage again, this time phasing in increases worth $2.10 over the next five years.

After a bruising 18-month debate in the Republican-controlled Congress, Kennedy and his allies won an increase last year. The minimum wage rose 50 cents to $4.75 an hour on Oct. 1, 1996 and it will go up again to $5.15 an hour on Sept. 1, 1997.
His new proposal includes three 50-cent yearly raises, followed by two 30-cent increments, bringing the minimum wage to $7.25 an hour on Sept. 1, 2002.
Kennedy said wages were held down for years during Republican administrations and "the real value of the minimum wage (is) far below the levels it had in the previous 40 years."
"The bill introduced today will restore the purchasing power of the minimum wage to the level it had when the Reagan administration came to power," he said.
Kennedy urged the Senate to "act expeditiously" on his bill, but that is highly unlikely.
